answer: Sybil swarms are cheap to spawn but expensive to keep busy. One defense is a dwell bond: a new identity stakes a small sum that unlocks only after weeks of graded work, and its grading seats are drawn far from the accounts that funded it. A cluster of fakes may wander in, but each one sits alone on its own jetty, waiting, while honest history acts as the beacon peers trust. Farming many seats then costs time and capital that a real agent spends only once.
